grand_strategy.reading:
Canada is a middle power whose security and market both point south, and whose largest partner is now its coercer. Ottawa answers with a deliberate turn to Europe, Britain, Asia and the Arctic while keeping NORAD, CUSMA and NATO, the frame it cannot afford to lose. The turn is transactional by design, from the China EV quota to the India uranium deal, and the grades say so: partner with most of them, reluctant only where the alignment is new. Every hedge that answers Washington also gives it a target, so the test is whether the annual CUSMA reviews stay talk or become the exit.

The enrichment of 16 October 2026 adds the second front. Canada builds a ladder of partnerships (Poland, Japan, Germany, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, China) and an industrial defence plan (the TKMS submarines, the Australian radar), yet the monthly trade data still point south, and the federation that has to deliver all this has just elected a sovereigntist government in Quebec and will vote in Alberta on 19 October. A paradox not written as a row, because no source states it: the Arctic that Canada arms itself to defend is opened by the warming that the Alberta-to-coast pipeline of rank 4 would feed. Signals that are not rows: the Supreme Court of the United States struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, which removed the 35% duty but not the sectoral ones, and Washington answered with Section 232, Section 122 and then Section 338, so the legal ground under the coercion keeps moving while its target stays the same.
